project.title: Mechanisms of Zero-Valent Iron, Ferrous Iron, and Ferric Iron in Enhancing Nitrogen Removal by the Heterotrophic Nitrification-Aerobic Denitrification Bacterium Alcaligenes sp. LJB3 through Regulation of Distinct Metabolic Pathways
project.description: Heterotrophic nitrification-aerobic denitrification (HN-AD) bacteria can concurrently conduct heterotrophic nitrification and aerobic denitrification in a single aerobic environment, achieving efficient nitrogen removal. Iron enhances electron transfer efficiency and promotes the rapid regeneration of reducing equivalents such as NADH. In this study, a HN-AD strain was isolated from micro-aerobic activated sludge and identified as Alcaligenes sp. LJB3. The mechanistic effects of different forms of iron-namely zero-valent iron (ZVI), Fe2+, and Fe3+ on this strain were investigated through their exogenous supplementation. The results showed that ZVI, Fe2+, and Fe3+ enhanced NH4+-N removal efficiency by 29.7%, 31.0%, and 30.0%, respectively, compared to the control. The different forms of iron elevated the NAD+/NADH ratio, reactive oxygen species and catalase activity. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that iron upregulated iron metabolism processes and stimulated cell-wall synthesis and cell-morphology regulation pathways. ZVI significantly upregulated the expression of sucA and odhB, which encode key enzymes (alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase) in the TCA cycle and nitrogen metabolism, thereby promoting glutamate synthesis via ammonium assimilation. Fe2+ increased the expression of genes involved in dissimilatory/assimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium, facilitating efficient nitrogen removal by coordinating the interconversion of NH4+-N and nitrate-nitrogen while alleviating toxicity from free ammonium and ROS. Fe3+ moderately elevated gene expression related to the TCA cycle and nitrogen metabolism, though its impact was less pronounced than that of ZVI and Fe2+. The study on the mechanism of iron enhanced HN-AD bacteria in removing NH4+-N is beneficial for the application and development of this technology in actual wastewater treatment.
